aldric.daily.001: Spring makes the readings jump. It could be the new growth, or whatever the new growth wakes up. I'm still working on that part.$h
aldric.daily.002: The instruments are busiest when it's hot. I thought the heat was interfering with them, but the spikes are too consistent.$h
aldric.daily.003: Autumn gives me the strangest readings. The leaves are falling, everything is settling down... except whatever I'm measuring.$h
aldric.daily.004: I expected the readings to settle under the snow. They haven't. At least the cold gives me an excuse to keep the kettle on.$h
aldric.daily.005: Mondays are for sorting notes. I tell myself that every week, then spend half the morning looking for a pencil.$h
aldric.daily.006: I found two accounts written forty years apart. They describe the same sound from the forest. Neither author knew the other.$h
aldric.daily.007: I was at the pond late again. The readings wouldn't settle, and I dislike leaving an unanswered question behind.$h
aldric.daily.008: I'm writing to the Institute today. The trick is making all this sound plausible without leaving out anything important.$h
aldric.daily.009: The Wizard passed me at the pond and pretended not to see me. At this point, I almost admire the consistency.$h
aldric.daily.010: I've spent the morning looking for a case like this one. So far, the closest comparison is a weather report from a hundred years ago.$h
aldric.daily.011: I try not to take readings on Sundays. I still think about them, of course. I'm better at making rules than following them.$h
aldric.daily.012: I tried cataloguing every odd noise around camp. The list became less useful when I realized half of them were just squirrels.$h
aldric.daily.013: Gunther lent me a stack of old town ledgers. The handwriting is dreadful, but the stories are worth deciphering.$h
aldric.daily.014: There's a patch of ground near the pond where my compass refuses to point north. I checked it with two compasses.$h
aldric.daily.015: I nearly sent the Institute my grocery list instead of my field notes. The filenames were more similar than I'd like to admit.$h
aldric.daily.016: I keep meaning to ask the Wizard what he makes of my readings. He keeps managing not to be wherever I am.$h
aldric.daily.017: Living in a tent makes it difficult to misplace things. You'd think that would have cured me of the habit.$h
aldric.daily.018: I bought fresh bread from the saloon. I didn't think I missed decent bread until I tried living on trail rations.$h
aldric.daily.019: I thought research would mean long hours in archives. It turns out it also means trying to dry wet notes over a camp stove.$h
aldric.daily.020: Some of the older records describe sounds just beyond the tree line. Always after dark. Nobody agrees on what made them.$u
aldric.daily.021: I like the pond in daylight. At night, I sometimes catch myself waiting for it to look back.$u
aldric.daily.022: My first report from the valley was twelve pages. The latest is thirty-one, and I still haven't written the conclusion.$h
aldric.daily.023: You can tell a great deal about a place by which questions people refuse to answer. I've learned to listen for the silence.$h
aldric.daily.024: I used to think a good theory explained every result. Lately I've been pleased if it explains half of them.$h
aldric.daily.025: I promised myself I wouldn't work today. Then I noticed something peculiar in yesterday's notes. So much for that.$h
aldric.daily.026: I haven't mentioned the figures at the pond in my reports. I'm still deciding whether that makes me cautious or cowardly.$u
aldric.daily.027: Marlon has been surprisingly helpful. He believes what he's seen, which is more than I can say for some of my colleagues.$h
aldric.daily.028: You don't have to tell me everything. Just promise you'll tell me if you think you're in danger.$u
aldric.daily.029: I went through the old accounts again. The dates are scattered, but the disappearances aren't. That bothers me.$u
aldric.daily.030: The Wizard has a talent for answering the question I didn't ask. I suspect he does it on purpose.$h
aldric.daily.031: I know I sound excited when I find something strange. It doesn't mean I've forgotten there are people involved.$u
aldric.daily.032: It's a strange comfort, having someone else know what I've seen. Thank you for that.$h
aldric.daily.033: I've been collecting the scattered accounts into one timeline. Each time I finish, I find a detail that changes it.$h
aldric.daily.034: You'd be surprised what an old tool can tell you about the person who used it. The smallest marks can matter.$h
aldric.daily.035: The more I understand what the practitioners tried to do, the less I envy them.$u
aldric.daily.036: I've stopped treating every anomaly as a separate problem. They're connected. I wish they weren't.$u
aldric.daily.037: I have enough material for three papers and not a single one that anyone would believe.$h
aldric.daily.038: If you come across anything unusual, keep it safe. I'd rather examine it with you than guess what it means.$h
aldric.daily.039: I used to measure progress by how many questions I could answer. Lately I measure it by whether we're still here.$h
aldric.daily.040: I keep the equipment ready, even on quiet days. It helps me think.$h
aldric.daily.041: I still have questions about this valley. I've begun to accept that I may never answer all of them.$h
aldric.daily.042: Sometimes I visit the pond without my instruments. It's a beautiful spot when I let myself notice.$h
aldric.daily.043: There's a section of my report titled 'Unresolved.' It may be the most truthful thing I've ever written.$h
aldric.daily.044: The Wizard nodded at me today. Not a word, just a nod. I'm counting it as progress.$h
aldric.daily.045: I thought solving a mystery would make it easier to sleep. Apparently my brain has other plans.$h
aldric.daily.046: You know, I came here looking for an explanation. I didn't expect to find a friend as well.$h
aldric.daily.047: Something on the western farmland gave my instruments quite a jolt recently. A remarkably precise one.$h
aldric.daily.048: Lately the spikes seem almost deliberate. That isn't a word I'd normally put in my notes, but nothing else fits.$h
aldric.daily.049: Whatever is causing this isn't somewhere far away. I'm beginning to think it's been under our feet all along.$u
aldric.daily.050: I've had to revise my calculations twice this week. Neither version is particularly reassuring.$u
aldric.daily.051: Those figures have been appearing at the pond more often. I can explain a faulty instrument. I can't explain them.$u
aldric.daily.052: My instruments have been quiet since the disturbance. I keep checking them. Part of me still expects the needles to move.$h
aldric.daily.053: The Wizard actually spoke with me. I took notes afterward, though I doubt he'd approve of my interpretation.$h
aldric.daily.054: I've decided to stay a while. The Institute can call it follow-up research. That's close enough to the truth.$h
aldric.daily.055: This is — yes. Thank you. I didn't expect this.$h
aldric.daily.057: That's kind of you, though it's not quite my preference.$h
aldric.daily.058: I appreciate the gesture, though this isn't something I'd have chosen.$h
aldric.name: Aldric
altar.002: You will find your learned rituals within.
altar.003: Give of your life's essence and you shall be given power over nature itself.
altar.004: Drink too deeply and suffer appropriately.
altar.005: Rituals will consume the needed regents on your person or adjacent chests.
altar.008: No rites have been revealed to you.
altar.026: Opens a passage to the Forgotten Temple.
altar.028: Ends the bond and removes Blood Debt.
boss.001: The red sigil keeps my body whole. Do you dare offer your blood and cut it loose?
boss.002: The anchor holds its body together. Touch the red sigil and offer 20 HP through the Ceremonial Dagger to break the binding.
boss.003: You need more health to sever the anchor. Eat or drink to restore your HP, then come back to the red sigil. You must have more than 20 HP.
boss.choice.01: The Unending asks why you have come.
boss.choice.03: I want to know what the cult sought.
boss.unendingfinalwords.01: No... the boundary was open. I could feel your world.
boss.unendingfinalwords.02: You cut my body loose from their chain. For an instant, I was free.
boss.unendingfinalwords.03: Do not mistake this silence for certainty. A wound leaves a scar.
boss.unendingfinalwords.04: I will remember the hand that closed it.
boss.unendingintroafterchoice.01: Their anchor holds me here, but it also keeps this body from dying. Break the chain, and you may have a chance to destroy me... before I am free.
boss.unendingintroafterchoice.02: So strike, little blood-worker. I have waited longer than your valley has had a name. I do not believe you can win before I am free.
boss.unendingintrobeforechoice.01: So. The little blood-worker has finally found the wound.
boss.unendingintrobeforechoice.02: That voice in your dreams was never mine. It belonged to one of those who opened this breach. It knew what waited here, and it led you anyway.
boss.unendingintrobeforechoice.03: The old families never worshipped me. They came to take my power, as if it were a thing they could carry home.
boss.unendingintrobeforechoice.04: They opened a way through the boundary. When they could not command what answered, they made a seal and an anchor to hold it.
boss.unendingintrobeforechoice.05: They buried the evidence, not because the work was finished, but because they feared what they had made.
boss.unendingintrobeforechoice.06: Your first rite cracked the seal. Every offering after that widened the breach. Blood Debt was never payment. It was recognition.
boss.unendingintrobeforechoice.07: The dreams began before you understood any of this. As your debt grew, the voices became harder to ignore.
boss.unendingintrobeforechoice.08: And now you stand before me with their diary, their dagger, and your scholar's field sample. Three little safeguards.
boss.unendingintrobeforechoice.09: The diary taught you how to call me. The sample steadied the passage. The dagger may yet cut what holds me.
boss.unendingintrobeforechoice.10: None of them can command me. That was the mistake your predecessors made.
boss.unendingretrydialogue.01: Back again, my little plaything? I almost respect you.
boss.unendingretrydialogue.02: Soon you will be dead, and the valley will be mine. You should have run like the rest of that silly cult.
dream.002:
You cannot see us.
Not yet.
Eyes are a recent invention.
What we are predates them considerably.
dream.003:
It has been watching this farm
for longer than this farm has existed.
dream.004:
You came here and planted things
and ate what grew
and did not ask what was already growing here
before you arrived.
dream.005:
Something was already here.
Something has always been here.
The valley is not empty land.
The valley is a mouth.
dream.006:
The altar is not something you found.
The altar is something that
has been waiting to be found.
By you.
Specifically.
dream.007:
It knew your name
before your parents chose it.
dream.008:
Welcome to the valley.
It has been expecting you
for quite some time.
It is very glad you finally arrived.
dream.009:
You will understand
what that means
eventually.
dream.011:
Not the altar. The altar is fine.
The altar is very pleased with you.
What you broke was underneath the altar.
A seal.
Something the old families built
when they decided to stop.
dream.012:
They poured everything they knew
into that seal.
They thought it would hold.
dream.013:
They were wrong.
You are the proof of this.
dream.014:
Something beneath this valley
shifted when you performed that ritual.
Not moved. Shifted.
The way something very large shifts
when it is waking up.
dream.016:
You are very small.
It noticed you anyway.
You should find that troubling.
dream.017:
The debt you carry is not financial.
It is not spiritual.
It is cellular.
Every drop of blood you spend at that altar
changes something in you
that does not change back.
dream.018:
It is pleased with the changes so far.
It has opinions about where they are going.
It has not shared those opinions yet.
It is enjoying the suspense.
dream.020:
There were witches here before you.
Not the storybook kind.
The real kind.
The kind that knew the valley's name before there were words to speak it.
dream.021:
They paid for what they knew
in the same currency you are spending.
Drop by drop.
Night by night.
Dream by dream.
dream.022:
Some of them are buried in your field.
You have walked over them.
You have grown things in the soil above them.
You have eaten what grew there.
This is how it maintains
continuity.
dream.023:
You've gone further than you intended.
You feel it now, don't you?
That certainty that something has changed.
The witches felt it too.
dream.025:
Of course you are.
So were they.
A leaf may choose how to turn,
but the wind decides
where it lands.
dream.027:
For now, perhaps.
The power is real.
So is the cost.
Something has been collecting
every drop you've offered.
One day it will ask for the rest.
dream.029:
There.
You can feel it after all.
Hold on to that feeling.
It may be the last warning
you recognize.
dream.030:
The blood you have spent at the altar
has gone somewhere specific.
Not metaphorically. Literally.
dream.031:
Something in this valley is drinking it.
It has been drinking from this valley
for longer than the valley has had a name.
And now it knows your taste.
dream.032:
It wants you to continue.
It is very interested
in what you will do next.
It has not been this interested
in anything
for a very long time.
dream.034:
Not through the altar.
Through you.
You have become a conduit
for something without a name
in any language still spoken.
dream.035:
The ones who named it are gone.
Most of them chose to go.
Some of them were helped.
dream.036:
Right now, in this moment,
something is using you
the way you use a window.
Looking out.
Seeing what is on the other side.
dream.037:
You gave it permission
every time you came back to the altar.
You did not know you were doing this.
This is why the agreement is not written down.
dream.038:
Do you understand
what you have become?
dream.040:
You did.
Every step.
Every ritual.
And it watched each choice.
You fascinate it.
Not as one person fascinates another,
but as a specimen fascinates
the hand holding the knife.
dream.042:
It is not inside your thoughts.
It looks through you
as sunlight passes through glass.
You opened the way yourself.
That is what made you useful.
dream.043: What do you want from me?
dream.044:
The same thing it has always wanted.
The same thing the seal was built to prevent.
You have been opening a door.
Something waits beyond it.
And when the threshold gives way,
it will need somewhere to arrive.
dream.045:
You will wake up
and the sun will be out
and none of this will seem real.
dream.046: And the altar will be there.
dream.047: And you will go to it.
dream.048:
Because you always do.
Because you were made to.
Because by now
you cannot tell the difference
between wanting to
and being unable
to stop.
dream.049:
It thinks this is beautiful.
It has always found inevitability beautiful.
This is one of the few things
you are beginning to have in common.
dream.050: You are lying on the altar.
dream.051: You do not remember getting there.
dream.052:
Your hands are open.
Your veins are open.
Something is learning how you work.
dream.053:
It watches your body struggle,
heal, and struggle again.
It wants to know how much
you can survive.
dream.055:
Not with your permission.
Permission is not required anymore.
dream.056: You wake knowing something you did not know before.
dream.057:
The knowledge is terrible.
You understand it anyway.
dream.058:
You understand how to open the vein
without killing what it feeds.
dream.059:
This knowledge was given to you.
It will expect something in return.
dream.060: The symbols hold still for you now.
dream.061:
They used to writhe.
They used to slide away from meaning
when you looked directly at them.
dream.062: Now they remain where you put them.
dream.063:
The lines close.
The angles balance.
The vessel does not crack.
dream.064: You have begun to understand the structure of it.
dream.065:
Each working is steadier now.
The blood follows your hand.
Or seems to.
dream.066: This is what control feels like.
dream.067: It is pleased that you believe this.
dream.068: Something vast is watching you refine the process.
dream.070: A careful hand makes a better instrument.
dream.071:
You wake with the certainty
that the rituals have become safer.
dream.072:
You also wake with the certainty
that safety was never the point.
dream.073: You are standing in your field.
dream.074:
Everything looks as it should.
The crops.
The soil.
The quiet.
dream.075: Something is trying to come through.
dream.076:
Not the altar.
Not the valley.
Through you.
dream.077:
You can feel where it would fit.
The shape it expects you to take.
The parts of you that have already made room.
dream.078: This is what the rituals were for.
dream.080:
You have been making yourself into something that can hold it.
Something that can survive the moment it arrives.
dream.081: It has been very patient with you.
dream.082:
It did not rush.
It did not force.
It let you choose every step.
dream.084:
You understand now why the debt is counted.
Why it is never erased.
Why it only accumulates.
dream.085: Each drop brought you closer to the shape it needs.
dream.086: Each ritual made the boundary thinner.
dream.087: There is something on the other side of that boundary.
dream.088: It is not the thing that has been speaking to you.
dream.089: That was only the part that could reach.
dream.090: This is what has been reaching.
dream.091: This is what has been waiting.
dream.092: This is what will come through.
dream.093: It does not have a name you could use.
dream.098: What comes next is not another working.
dream.100: And you are where it will arrive.
dream.102:
There is no pressure.
No presence.
No voice.
dream.104: You can feel where it used to be.
dream.105:
A shape.
A space.
A connection.
dream.110: There is less fear in the silence now.
dream.114:
You are at the altar.

You are also somewhere else.
dream.115:
The stone is warm.
Warmer than it has ever been.
It knows what you are doing.
dream.116:
The valley knows.
You can feel it in the roots beneath your feet.
In the dark soil that fed you for so long.
dream.117:
Something is watching.
Not with hunger this time.
With something that might be,
if it were capable of such things,
respect.
dream.118:
You have been here before.
In dreams.
In the dark at the edge of each morning.
You have stood at this threshold and looked through it.
dream.119:
This time you are not looking through.
This time you are closing it.
dream.120:
It speaks.
One last time.
Not to convince you.
Not to offer anything.
Just—
dream.121:
We know what you are doing.

We know why.

We want you to know that we are not angry.
dream.122:
We were here long before you.
We will remain when you are gone.
But you need not remain with us.
dream.123:
You were the most interesting one
in a very long while.
dream.125:
The bond pulls as you cut it.
Not resisting.
Just—
the weight of everything it held.
dream.126:
All the dreams.
All the debt.
All the nights something moved through you
while you slept.
dream.127:
You let it go.

It lets you go.
dream.128: The altar goes cold beneath your hands.
dream.129:
Not dead.
Just—
no longer a door.
dream.130:
You are standing in your field.

There is nothing pressing through the soil.
dream.131:
The silence is yours.

All of it.

For the first time.
event.aldricmanager.002: I apologize — I know this is abrupt. You're the farmer on the northwest property?$h
event.aldricmanager.003: Dr. Aldric Voss. Forensic alchemist, consulting for the Institute for Anomalous Resonance Studies.$h#$b#I'll be in the valley for a while — indeterminate duration. I've set up a field camp in the forest; easier to stay close to the readings.
event.aldricmanager.004: I'm not here about your farm specifically. There have been unusual resonance readings concentrated in this region for several years. I'm here to identify the source.
event.aldricmanager.005: If you notice anything unusual — anything you wouldn't know how to explain — I'd appreciate a firsthand account. People living in a place tend to notice what instruments miss.$h
event.aldricmanager.007: I've been here most of the morning. Gunther's been generous.$h
event.aldricmanager.009: Within very specific parameters. Yes.$h#$b#This valley has an unusual artifact density for a settlement of this size and age. The pre-civilization record shows organized, structured practice — not folk magic, not occasional ceremony. Generational. Sustained.
event.aldricmanager.010: The same group appears to have been active here for several generations before the town was incorporated. And then they stopped. Abruptly. No gradual decline, no documented dispersal. Just — cessation.$h
event.aldricmanager.011: That's the question keeping me here. Something caused a complete discontinuation. That kind of thing leaves a mark.$h#$b#I intend to find it.
event.aldricmanager.012: Dr. Voss. I'm sure our guest has other things to look at.
event.aldricmanager.013: Right. Yes. Apologies.$h#$b#I tend to think out loud. If the valley's history interests you — genuinely — come find me. I have more notes than I have people willing to read them.
event.aldricmanager.014: Careful with the light there — this piece has been unlabeled for eleven years and I intend to finally change that today.$h
event.aldricmanager.015: The spiral pattern. Compare it to what I sketched from the dagger.$h
event.aldricmanager.016: Ah, perfect timing! Come look at this. Doctor Voss believes he's identified the maker's mark on one of our oldest unprovenanced pieces.$h
event.aldricmanager.017: This shard came in decades before I took the position. No documentation on where it was found, no attribution, nothing. It's sat in a drawer labeled 'miscellaneous, spring collection' for longer than I've been curator.$h
event.aldricmanager.018: The knotwork matches the dagger's crossguard, tine for tine. Same hand, or at minimum the same tradition.$h
event.aldricmanager.019: Do you understand what this means for the collection? A properly attributed piece, tied to an actual historical practice, with physical corroboration. This is the best afternoon I've had at this desk in years.$h
event.aldricmanager.020: I'd like to formally note the connection in my own records, with your permission. Off the museum ledger, for now.$h
event.aldricmanager.021: Granted, of course. Though I insist on being the first to know when you're ready to make it official. A discovery like this deserves proper documentation, not a footnote.$h
event.aldricmanager.022: Oh— hello again, by the way. Your artifact donations made this possible, you know. I hope you realize that.$h
event.aldricmanager.023: ...and I never told anyone. Who exactly was I going to tell? 'Excuse me, the woods have been acting strange, and I would know, I live in them'?$h
event.aldricmanager.024: That's precisely the kind of testimony that gets dismissed for the wrong reasons. Please, continue.$h
event.aldricmanager.025: Good, you're here. Linus has been telling me something I think you'll want to hear too.$h
event.aldricmanager.026: There's a stretch of ground past the old stump, west side. Nothing grows evenly there. It's not soil quality — I've tested that myself, over the years. Things just grow wrong. Spirals, some of them. Never toward the light. Always toward that one spot.
event.aldricmanager.027: The animals know it too. Deer go around it. Even the foxes, and foxes go through anything.
event.aldricmanager.028: How long has this been happening?$h
event.aldricmanager.029: Longer than you've been in the valley. Longer than I've had this tent, and I've had this tent a long time.$h
event.aldricmanager.030: Never reported it. Who reports something like that? A hermit telling the mayor his trees are growing wrong? I'd have gotten a wellness check, not a scientist.$h
event.aldricmanager.031: You have my genuine gratitude for telling me now. This is exactly the kind of long-term observation the written record can't give me.$h
event.aldricmanager.032: Didn't do it for gratitude. Did it because you asked without making me feel foolish for the answer. Not everyone manages that.$h
event.aldricmanager.033: I really don't see why this needs to be in writing anywhere, Doctor. Some things are better left in the filing cabinet, if you follow me.$u
event.aldricmanager.034: I'm not asking for public disclosure, Mayor. I'm asking for accuracy. There's a difference.$h
event.aldricmanager.035: Oh— hello. I suppose you're part of this too, given the doctor tells me it's your land in question.
event.aldricmanager.036: Lewis has been kind enough to let me look through the old land record ledgers. I asked specifically about parcels that changed hands without a sale.$h
event.aldricmanager.037: There's exactly one in that ledger from that era. Land reassigned to the township, 'due to abandonment, prior occupants unaccounted for.' No name of who requested the reassignment. No follow-up entry, ever — which is unusual. We're thorough about follow-up entries.
event.aldricmanager.038: The parcel boundaries. Do they overlap with the current farm?$h
event.aldricmanager.039: ...They do. Not entirely, but the northern boundary line runs directly through what's now your property.$h#$b#I'd rather this stayed between us for now. The valley doesn't need another reason for tourists to ask uncomfortable questions at the Egg Festival.
event.aldricmanager.040: Understood. And appreciated, Lewis. I know this wasn't an easy record to hand over.$h
event.aldricmanager.041: It wasn't a record I enjoyed finding, if I'm honest. I've been mayor a long time. I'd have preferred this valley's paperwork stayed boring.$h
event.aldricmanager.042: Oh, you're sweet to ask, dear, but it's really just an old rhyme. Nothing scholarly about it.$h
event.aldricmanager.043: Folk rhymes are exactly what I'm interested in, Evelyn. The scholarly record and the oral one rarely agree, and I trust yours more some days.$h
event.aldricmanager.044: Oh, hello dear! Come in, come in — I was just about to embarrass myself in front of the doctor here.$h
event.aldricmanager.045: My grandmother used to say this to me at bedtime, if I was misbehaving. I always thought it was meant to be scary, the way grown-ups make up scary things to get children to sleep.$h
event.aldricmanager.046: 'Mind the patient one beneath the hill, it does not forget, it does not forgive. Feed it kindly, feed it true, or it will come and collect from you.'
event.aldricmanager.048: Goodness, you look pale, Doctor. It's only a silly old rhyme. I haven't thought about it in decades.$h
event.aldricmanager.049: 'Feed it kindly, or it will come and collect.' That phrasing. I need to write this down exactly as you said it.$u
event.aldricmanager.050: Well, if it's that important to you, of course. Though I can't imagine why a scholar would want an old woman's bedtime rhyme.$h
event.aldricmanager.051: Would either of you like a cookie? I just took a batch out, and I do hate for scary talk to go with an empty stomach.$h
event.aldricmanager.052: Good timing. Sit down if you have a moment.
event.aldricmanager.053: I've built a working profile of the group that practiced in this region. I've been calling them 'the practitioners' — they didn't use a name, or none that made it into any account I've found.
event.aldricmanager.054: Mostly local families, passing what they knew from parent to child. They kept outsiders away. I haven't found a single account of someone being invited in.$h
event.aldricmanager.055: Blood-centered practice. Accounts are consistent across independent sources — offerings, transaction-based, tied to the land itself. Crop yields in the area they occupied were significantly above regional average for the entire period of their activity.$h#$b#Something was responding to them.
event.aldricmanager.056: Then there's a letter. A man named Halwick, about eighty years ago — he describes what he calls 'the awakening of something patient.' The letter ends mid-sentence.$h
event.aldricmanager.057: The family line vanishes from valley records in the same year. Eleven people, gone in a single season with no destination recorded.$h#$b#This keeps repeating across sources. The practitioners didn't drift away. They left quickly, all at once, in ways that were clearly unplanned.$h#$b#People don't all disappear at once without a reason. I want to find out what happened.
event.aldricmanager.058: I didn't expect company out here tonight.
event.aldricmanager.059: I come here most evenings. The readings near this pond are the highest in the valley. There's a directionality to them — like a signal with a source. I'm very close to triangulating it.$h
event.aldricmanager.060: The Wizard has been diplomatically unhelpful. He clearly knows something. He's made that apparent by how carefully he avoids saying it.$h
event.aldricmanager.061: I've also been seeing figures. In the treeline — just there, to the west.
event.aldricmanager.062: Five times since I started monitoring this location.$h#$b#Always the same hour window — dusk, never earlier. Always the same configuration. Always facing east, toward the pond.
event.aldricmanager.063: They don't move. No ritual action I can observe. No communication between them. They stand, and then they're gone.$h#$b#I've tried to approach twice. The first time they vanished before I crossed the pond. The second time I couldn't find a crossing quickly enough.$h
event.aldricmanager.064: The resonance readings spike every time they appear. Not slightly — significantly. As though their presence amplifies whatever is already active here.$h#$b#I've described them to two colleagues who specialize in organized practice. Neither recognized the configuration.$h
event.aldricmanager.066: I've filed them as persons of interest. That's the category I use for things I've observed and cannot currently classify.$h
event.aldricmanager.067: The readings have been escalating for weeks. Something is more active than when I arrived — more attentive is the word I keep using in my personal notes, even though it isn't a scientific word.$h#$b#If you've noticed anything unusual around here, I'd genuinely want to know.
event.aldricmanager.068: ...and that's the last anyone heard of them. Whole families, gone inside a season. Nobody in town much liked to talk about it, even years after.$s
event.aldricmanager.069: You're certain of the timeline? Within the season, not the year?$h
event.aldricmanager.070: Certain as I can be. I was young, but you don't forget something like that.$s
event.aldricmanager.071: Oh — didn't see you there. Come in, come in.$h
event.aldricmanager.072: Good timing, actually. Marlon was just telling me something relevant to my research — he knew the old families this valley used to have. The ones I've been reading about in the archives.$h
event.aldricmanager.073: Knew of them, mostly. My father did business with a couple of them, back before I ever picked up a sword. Kept to themselves. Odd hours. The kind of odd you learn not to ask about, if you're smart.$h
event.aldricmanager.074: Marlon's account lines up with three separate written sources I've cross-referenced. That's the first living corroboration I've had for any of this.$h
event.aldricmanager.075: Living corroboration. I like that. Makes me sound important.$h
event.aldricmanager.076: You are, for the purposes of this conversation.$h
event.aldricmanager.077: Well — good luck with whatever you're chasing, Doc.$h
event.aldricmanager.078: Thank you for stopping by. It's a nicer interruption than most.$h
event.aldricmanager.079: I'm going to trace the second signal and compare it with the surviving accounts. Something happened to those families when the pattern reached this stage. I intend to find out what.$u
event.aldricmanager.080: Keep a record of every rite and every change in your dreams. If something answers before you ask, I need to know immediately.$u#$b#This is no longer just a question of what the altar does for you. Other people live in this valley.$u
event.aldricmanager.081: I'm not going anywhere. And before you ask, yes, I'm frightened too. I regard that as a reasonable response to the data.$h
event.aldricmanager.082: When we spoke at the beach, I told you I knew about the altar. I didn't tell you how much it worried me. I wanted evidence before I frightened us both.$u
event.aldricmanager.083: Now I have it. Every surge I've measured at your farm is followed by a second pulse. Different location, same signature. As though something is answering the first.$u
event.aldricmanager.084: I compared the sequence with what survives of Halwick's records. The same paired readings appear in the weeks before those families vanished. The intervals grew shorter then. They're growing shorter now.$u
event.aldricmanager.085: The altar isn't the source. It's a point of contact. Every time you reach toward whatever is on the other end, it has another chance to reach back.$u
event.aldricmanager.086: I am not asking whether you're involved. We settled that. What I need to know is what you intend to do now that we have reason to believe the other side is getting closer.$u
event.aldricmanager.087: Then we investigate rather than speculate. I'll follow the readings; you tell me what happens when you perform a rite. The pattern has a cause. We can work toward finding it.$h
event.aldricmanager.088: You may be right about your own actions. What concerns me is that you cannot control the answer. Those families believed they could manage it too, right up until the records stop.$u
event.aldricmanager.089: I didn't sleep much. I spent most of the night comparing your rubbings from the temple against the two artifacts you brought me.$u
event.aldricmanager.090: I was wrong about both of them.$h#$b#Not completely wrong. Worse than that — incomplete.
event.aldricmanager.091: The damaged diary isn't simply an account of the rites. It's a working record of one particular procedure: how they opened the correspondence, how they held it stable, and where the process began to fail.$u
event.aldricmanager.092: And the dagger wasn't just ceremonial preparation. The wear pattern matches the marks around the anchor described in the temple. It was used to sever the thing that held a manifestation here.$u
event.aldricmanager.093: That changes the old cult's story. They weren't worshipping The Unending. They were trying to force it into a controlled manifestation, cut its anchor, and take something from it before it could fully establish itself.$u
event.aldricmanager.094: They failed. The breach they left behind never closed. And every ritual you've performed since then has been feeding the same resonance.$u#$b#Doing nothing is not neutral anymore.
event.aldricmanager.095: So I'm giving these back to you, along with something else. They were evidence; now they're tools.$h
event.aldricmanager.096: There's a third implement. I recovered a field sample near Node 7, and its resonance matches the fluctuations in the temple records. It may be the only way to stabilize the breach long enough to sever the anchor.$u
event.aldricmanager.097: Take all three with you when you perform the Call. The diary gives you the sequence, the dagger cuts the anchor, and the sample holds the connection steady. None of them should be sacrificed.$u
event.aldricmanager.098: I'm not telling you this is safe. I'm telling you that waiting for the breach to choose its own time and place may be worse.$u#$b#If you're going to do this, choose the conditions yourself.
event.aldricmanager.099: I was hoping you'd stop by. I've been trying to find the right words since the readings changed. The notes aren't helping.$h
event.aldricmanager.100: After everything that happened, the readings simply... stopped. For the first time since I arrived, the instruments are quiet. I don't know whether to feel relieved.$h
event.aldricmanager.101: I have a theory about what happened, but I can't put it in my report. How would I even begin to explain it? They'd think I'd lost my mind. Some days I'm not entirely sure they're wrong.$h
event.aldricmanager.102: The valley feels different now.$h#$b#I suspect you've noticed that too.
event.aldricmanager.103: I'm staying. The Institute will call it continued monitoring for resonance aftershocks, which is technically accurate.$h#$b#There's also the Wizard. He knows considerably more about this region than he's chosen to share, and I've decided I'm going to make friends with him.$h#$b#He seems committed to making this difficult. I find that motivating rather than discouraging.
event.aldricmanager.104: I'll be around. I think you know where to find me.$h
event.aldricmanager.105: Oh — welcome. Forgive the state of things. Field conditions don't leave much room for tidiness.$h
event.aldricmanager.106: I picked this spot for the sightline to the pond and the tree cover. Neither the Guild nor the museum gave me anything close to a clean baseline reading — too much ambient interference from foot traffic.$h
event.aldricmanager.107: It's not glamorous. A tent, a table, and more paperwork than either can comfortably hold. But it's quiet, and quiet is what the instruments need.$h#$b#You're welcome here, if you don't mind the mess.
event.aldricmanager.108: Careful — I've got readings sorted by significance on the ground. The system only makes sense to me, which I recognize is not a strength.$h
event.aldricmanager.109: Forensic alchemist. It's a smaller field than it sounds. Most of my colleagues work insurance fraud or estate disputes. I specialize in things that don't have a tidy legal category.$h
event.aldricmanager.110: The Institute assigns me to sites with unusually persistent anomalous activity. This valley qualified before I'd even finished reading the file.$h
event.aldricmanager.111: It's solitary work, mostly. You measure things other people can't see, and then you write reports that other people don't read.$s#$b#I don't say that as a complaint. Just an observation. I'm good at observations.
event.aldricmanager.112: Anyway. Thank you for coming back. It's a nicer interruption than most.$h
event.aldricmanager.113: You've caught me on a slow evening. Sit, if you'd like. There's a crate that's marginally more comfortable than the others.$h
event.aldricmanager.114: I don't usually explain why I do this work. It invites questions I don't enjoy answering.$h#$b#I'll make an exception.
event.aldricmanager.115: My aunt raised me for several years. She kept a journal of things she couldn't explain — sounds in the walls, objects that moved, a light in the orchard that didn't belong to any lamp we owned.$h
event.aldricmanager.116: Everyone told her it was nothing. Stress, imagination, an old house settling. She stopped mentioning it out loud, but she never stopped writing it down.$h#$b#She passed before I was old enough to ask her the right questions.
event.aldricmanager.117: I became the kind of person who measures things, instead of the kind who dismisses them. I tell myself that's for her. I think that's mostly true.$h
event.aldricmanager.118: This valley is the closest I've come to readings that resemble what she described. That's not entirely a professional interest anymore. I wanted you to know that.$h
event.aldricmanager.119: Thank you for listening. I don't offer that story often.$h
event.aldricmanager.120: Evening. I was hoping you'd turn up. There's something I wanted to share with you.$h
event.aldricmanager.121: I know more than I have been telling you. I decided today is the day that stops.$u
event.aldricmanager.122: I know about the altar. A sacrificial altar produces an energy signature. Yours matches one.
event.aldricmanager.123: And I know something has been reaching out to you in your dreams. I don't know what it has shown you, or what it has said. You look exhausted. Have you been seeing things when you're awake, too?$u
event.aldricmanager.124: Whatever you've found is powerful. I can see why you'd want to keep using it. But I'm worried about what it's doing to you.$u
event.aldricmanager.125: I am not going to tell you to stop. I don't think you would anyway. What I will tell you is to keep going carefully. Document everything. Do not assume you understand the terms simply because you have agreed to them.
event.aldricmanager.126: You are not doing this alone anymore. That is the part I actually wanted you to hear.$h
event.aldricmanager.127: I want to understand this, but not at the cost of losing you to it. If something changes, come to me. You won't have to explain why.
event.aldricmanager.128: The readings peaked at 2:17 this morning. Higher than anything I've recorded since I arrived. And then — nothing. Clean baseline.$h
event.aldricmanager.129: I've been standing here since 2:40. I wasn't sure whether to knock.$h
event.aldricmanager.130: You're going to do it. Confront whatever is anchoring the anomaly. I've known that since I read the diary.$h#$b#I'm not going to tell you not to. That's not why I'm here.
event.aldricmanager.131: I want to say something first, as someone who has been watching this from the outside and has a professional framework for what I've observed.$h
event.aldricmanager.132: The pattern I keep documenting in long-term practitioners — the escalation, the rationalizations, the debt that accumulates faster than it clears — that's not weakness. It's a specific kind of cognitive trap. The system is designed to make continuation feel more reasonable than stopping.$h
event.aldricmanager.133: I'm asking you — clinically, not as a judgment — whether you are choosing this, or whether the choosing was done some time ago and you've been executing ever since.$h
event.aldricmanager.134: Good. That's the answer I hoped for, and I almost believe you.$h
event.aldricmanager.135: I know. That took something to say.$h
event.aldricmanager.136: Either way — I'm not going to be there with you. That's your decision to make. If I came with you, I suspect I'd only make it harder.$h
event.aldricmanager.137: What I can do is give you this.$h
event.aldricmanager.138: Node 7 resonance sample — the highest reading I collected, from the center of the pond on the night the cultists last appeared. My working hypothesis is that it's the same frequency as whatever you'll be facing.$h#$b#I don't know exactly what it will do in the context of your ritual. I wanted you to have something I could offer, even if I can't go with you.
event.aldricmanager.139: When you come back — and I expect you to — I'll be at the camp.$h#$b#The kettle will be on.
event.choices.001: I'll keep using it. I want answers.
event.choices.005: What will you do with what we left?
event.choices.006: I'll end this before it gets through.
event.choices.007: I'll take the power you couldn't.
event.modentry.001: So you've brought them. I don't usually have dreams like this, but it was like I was being commanded to make this. Just give me a moment and I'll forge this and put an end to it.
event.modentry.002: There. I don't know what I just made... but I think the dream can finally leave me alone.
event.modentry.004: ...$3#$b#I recognize the temptation. Power that answers quickly is always difficult to refuse.$3#$b#But I have never seen this strain of magic before. It does not belong to any school I know. It has structure, but no lineage.$3
event.modentry.005: I will consult my books. Until I know more, proceed carefully.$3#$b#And if it begins to feel as though it wants something from you... assume that it does.$3
event.modentry.006: I have been aware of something beneath this valley for years. I kept my distance from it deliberately.$3#$b#What you have been doing has made that distance harder to maintain.$3
event.modentry.007: It is not dormant. It is patient. And it has begun to feel less patient.$3#$b#I can sense it from here. It is large. And what I sense from it — if I am being precise about it — is hunger.$3
event.modentry.008: I am not telling you to stop.$3#$b#But I want you to understand something. Whatever is beneath this valley is not simply a source of power. It has attention. It has appetite.$3#$b#Consider what you are building toward. Power always carries a cost. Make sure you understand what you are paying before you find out what the final bill looks like.$3
event.modentry.010: The construction is consistent with what I have been reading about. Pre-settlement. The hide used for the drum face is from an animal species that no longer exists in this region.$h
event.modentry.011: I wasn't aware you had expertise in pre-Pelican Town material culture, Dr. Voss.
event.modentry.012: I don't. But I have spent three months reading every account of this valley's pre-settlement period I could find. This drum appears in several of them.$h#$b#The families who were active on the western farmland used drums in their rituals. The accounts are specific about timing — the drum marked the beginning and end of whatever they were doing at the site.$h
event.modentry.015: The accounts also note that crop yields in the surrounding area were significantly above regional average for the entire period the families were active. Whatever they were doing, the land responded to it.$h#$b#Then they left. The yields normalized. The drum presumably ended up in the ground.$h
event.modentry.016: I would very much like to keep that for the collection, if the farmer is willing.
event.modentry.017: That's between you and the farmer.$h#$b#What I needed from it I already have.
event.modentry.018: Is that— may I see that?$u
event.modentry.019: A ceremonial dagger. The etching on the hilt matches the pattern from the account I mentioned — this was used in the rites themselves, not for harm. A focus, the same way your altar focuses intent into ritual.
event.modentry.020: Look at the spiral work along the crossguard. That's not decoration — it's a repeating knot pattern. I've seen fragments of it before, on pottery shards Gunther has cataloged as unprovenanced. Nobody could say what it meant. Now I can.$h
event.modentry.021: Not every practitioner would have carried one of these. The organization I described to you — generational, insular — it had structure. Roles. This belonged to someone specific. A keeper, or a reader. Someone trusted with the actual mechanics of the rite, not just attendance at it.
event.modentry.022: As for 'not for harm' — I mean that clinically, not sentimentally. There's no residue in the fuller, no wear pattern consistent with cutting flesh. Whatever this cut, it was thread, or herb bundles, or offerings. Ceremonial preparation. The harm in these rites was never the blade's job.
event.modentry.023: Where did you find this? Never mind — it doesn't matter. What matters is it's real.$h#$b#I'd like to hold onto this, if you don't mind — I can examine it properly back at camp.
event.modentry.024: It's strange, holding something this old that's this well-preserved. Most artifacts this age have decayed past usefulness. This looks like it was cared for, right up until the moment it wasn't.$s
event.modentry.025: Thank you for bringing this to me.$h
event.modentry.026: ...You found it. I didn't actually expect you to.$u
event.modentry.027: Damaged, but legible in places — enough to confirm what the account only implied. Someone was documenting the rites as they happened, not reconstructing them after the fact. That's rarer than you'd think.
event.modentry.028: No full name. Just an initial — M. — repeated at the close of every entry, the way someone signs off when they assume only they will ever read it back.
event.modentry.029: The early entries are procedural. Almost clinical, honestly — I recognize the instinct. Dates, quantities, what was offered and when. The kind of record someone keeps when they still believe they're in control of what they're documenting.
event.modentry.030: That changes partway through. The handwriting gets tighter. Shorter sentences. One entry says only, 'it is heavier again, and I have told no one.' Whatever this cost M., they stopped writing about the ritual itself and started writing about carrying it.$s
event.modentry.031: I recognize that shift too. I would rather not say from where.$s
event.modentry.032: It reminds me of my aunt's journal, if I'm honest. Different hand, different century, same instinct — write it down before someone convinces you it wasn't real.$s
event.modentry.033: I'd like time with this. I'll let you know what I find.
event.templemanager.001: You were transported? Not a dream, not a vision — physically somewhere else?$u
event.templemanager.002: And the stonework reacted to you before you performed anything there. That is the part I want you to repeat very carefully.$u
event.templemanager.003: I have fragments in my notes that describe a sanctuary the old practitioners stopped naming near the end. I assumed it was metaphorical. I may have been wrong.$h
event.templemanager.004: Perform the passage again when you're ready. I want to go with you.$u#$b#For the record, that sentence makes me deeply uncomfortable.$h
event.templemanager.005: I'm not volunteering to lead the expedition. You are clearly the key the place recognizes. I'll come long enough to take baseline readings, then I'm going back to camp where I can compare them against my notes. You go deeper alone.$h
event.templemanager.006: And if a centuries-old blood cult built a door that asks you a question, please do me the courtesy of thinking before you answer it.$h
event.templemanager.007: All right. I'm going to say this once so I can spend the rest of the day pretending I didn't: I am nervous.$h
event.templemanager.008: The masonry is older than the records I brought with me. The residue isn't. Something in this structure is still active.$u
event.templemanager.009: And you were right. The threshold spiked the moment you arrived. Before blood. Before an incantation. It recognized you.$u
event.templemanager.010: I've got enough for a baseline. I'm taking these readings back to camp before this place decides to react to me too. You go on. Bring me rubbings, fragments, exact wording — anything I can compare against the records.$h
event.templemanager.011: If you find the source of the dreams, do not assume it is pleased to see you simply because it invited you.$u#$b#When you're done, go home and get some sleep. I need the night to compare these readings against my notes. I'll find you tomorrow.$h

Dreams are when the distance between us grows thin.^^No signature. The ink is slightly warm.
mail.MailQuestAncientDrum.body: Farmer,^^I have been cataloguing artifact finds from this region and cross-referencing them with the accounts I have collected about the practitioners.^^One item keeps appearing in the written record — a drum. The accounts describe it as ceremonial, used during the period of anomalous crop yields. If you have found an Ancient Drum while working your land, I would like to examine it at the museum where Gunther can provide additional context.^^Bring it to me there when you have one.^^—Dr. Aldric Voss^^
mail.MailQuestArtifacts.body: Farmer,^^Going back through the account that led me to the drum, I found two more references I had missed the first time through — a ceremonial dagger and a diary. Both are described as belonging to the same time period and the same practitioners.^^I do not know where either ended up. If you happen across anything matching that description while you are out digging — the forest, the beach, wherever your work takes you — I would like to see it. No particular hurry. Just keep an eye out.^^—Dr. Aldric Voss^^
mail.MailQuestSample.body: Farmer,^^My instruments recorded an anomaly last night near your farm. The readings were significant — stronger than anything I have recorded since arriving in the valley.^^I have a theory about its source, but I need something I can examine. If you have any void essence on hand, I would appreciate the opportunity to run a spectral analysis.^^I will be at my usual spots. You know where to find me.^^—Dr. Aldric Voss^^
mail.MailSeveranceLetter: Farmer,^^I have been observing your recent actions with great unease.^^What you confronted beneath this valley is older than any record I possess. Something has pressed against the boundary between worlds for longer than our records can tell us.^^You have done what few in any age could: you drove it back. For that, you have my gratitude.^^Yet I do not believe your connection to it is entirely gone. Such forces leave impressions, and impressions can become invitations if left unattended.^^I have written down a rite I once swore I would leave unrecorded. It is called the Rite of Severance. It will not strip you of the knowledge or power you now wield, but it may cut the claim that ancient darkness still holds upon you.^^I have placed the instructions within your Dark Tome. Read it carefully, and decide whether you wish to close this chapter.^^—M. Rasmodius^^
mail.MailWizardAfterSeverance: Farmer,^^I felt it last night.^^A silence I have never heard in this valley before. I have spent years studying events like this in theory. I have never been close enough to feel one until now.^^I want to be honest with you. I do not fully understand what you did out there, or what it cost you to do it. The records I have of the old families do not describe anyone who reached the point you have and then chose this particular exit.^^Most of them did not choose anything after a certain point. They simply ceased to be.^^I think that says something about you. I am not certain yet what it says. I would like to speak with you in person, if you are willing, when you feel ready for company.^^The valley is quieter this morning. I had forgotten what it felt like before whatever was beneath it woke up.^^It is a strange thing to be grateful for.^^—M. Rasmodius^^[#]A Note from the Tower
mail.MailWizardAura: Your aura has shifted.^^A heavy feeling has settled over your farm, as though the land itself is waiting to swallow you whole.^^The altar is no doubt giving you power you have never seen. It can be intoxicating.^^Proceed carefully.^^—M. Rasmodius
mail.MailWizardAuraAlchemy: Your aura has shifted.^^A heavy feeling has settled over your farm, as though the land itself is waiting to swallow you whole.^^The altar is no doubt giving you power you have never seen. It can be intoxicating.^^If you insist on continuing, alchemical reagents and properly prepared potions may help control some of the more unpredictable effects of this blood magic.^^Do not mistake control for safety.^^—M. Rasmodius
mail.MailWizardConcern: The forces you have begun to disturb are unfamiliar even to me.^^There is a hunger behind these rituals. With each offering, it grows more attentive.^^You may already have awakened something that cannot easily be put back to sleep. Proceed with great caution.^^—M. Rasmodius
mail.MailWizardUnease: You have done something you do not understand.^^I felt it from the tower.^^I know you possess a book of dark knowledge.^^Bring the tome to me. Do not continue experimenting blindly.^^—M. Rasmodius

ritual.BlackSunPact.description: Seal your pact beneath a lightless sun. Strength answers the call, and the altar remembers your promise.
ritual.BlackSunPact.name: Pact of the Black Sun
ritual.BloodWard.description: Trace protective sigils in blood. Your defenses strengthen, and harmful effects have less hold on you until morning.
ritual.BloodWard.name: Blood Ward
ritual.CallTheUnending.description: Open the breach and confront The Unending. The old cult tried to claim its power; their anchor may be the key to ending what they began.
ritual.CallTheUnending.name: Call of The Unending
ritual.CrimsonHarvest.description: Offer blood to the furrows and the blade alike. The harvest thrives, but something beneath the soil answers too.
ritual.CrimsonHarvest.name: Crimson Harvest
ritual.EternalNight.description: Draw upon an older darkness. Combat, speed, and luck rise sharply until morning.
ritual.EternalNight.name: Pact of Eternal Night
ritual.HarvestMoon.description: Draw the dark moon into root and leaf. Your farming and foraging improve until morning.
ritual.HarvestMoon.name: Rite of the Harvest Moon
ritual.HellfireInfusion.description: A volatile infusion that sharpens your combat instincts and lends unnatural force to every strike for the day.
ritual.HellfireInfusion.name: Hellfire Infusion
ritual.HollowFeast.description: Feed the soil with a forbidden offering. The crops flourish, and the hunger beneath them deepens.
ritual.HollowFeast.name: Hollow Feast
ritual.MoonlitAbundance.description: Call buried riches toward your hands and push your stamina beyond its limits. The earth gives freely, for now.
ritual.MoonlitAbundance.name: Moonlit Abundance
ritual.MoonveilDraught.description: Brewed beneath moonlight, this draught steadies your hand while fishing and turns chance slightly in your favor for the day.
ritual.MoonveilDraught.name: Moonveil Draught
ritual.NightmareVeil.description: Borrow a predator's speed and instinct from the darkness. It asks only that you leave a little of yourself behind.
ritual.NightmareVeil.name: Nightmare Veil
ritual.OpenVein.description: Trade pain for brutal strength. The altar remembers every wound, even after it closes.
ritual.OpenVein.name: Rite of the Open Vein
ritual.PhilosophersRite.description: The pinnacle of alchemical blood magic. Every skill surges simultaneously for one day.
ritual.PhilosophersRite.name: Philosopher's Blood Rite
ritual.RedPassage.description: Follow a path remembered by blood to the forgotten sanctuary of the old practitioners.
ritual.RedPassage.name: The Red Passage
ritual.RiteOfAbundance.description: Offer a fragment of the earth's buried wealth. Your stamina, mining skill, and reach for nearby items increase for the day.
ritual.RiteOfAbundance.name: Rite of Abundance
ritual.RiteOfSeverance.description: Cut the last thread binding you to The Unending. Your Blood Debt is cleared, but the knowledge you gained remains.
ritual.RiteOfSeverance.name: Rite of Severance
ritual.SanguinePact.description: Bind blood and shadow together. Your blows strike harder, and your combat skill rises until morning.
ritual.SanguinePact.name: Sanguine Pact
ritual.VeilOfShadows.description: Let the shadows guide your steps and strikes, sharpening your speed, luck, and combat skill for the day.
ritual.VeilOfShadows.name: Veil of Shadows
ritual.WanderingSoul.description: Bind a wandering soul to quicken your steps, improve your luck, and draw distant items nearer for the day.
ritual.WanderingSoul.name: Rite of the Wandering Soul
ritual.WyrmbloodTincture.description: Steep dragon root and fang in blood to sharpen your fighting instincts and add force to your strikes for the day.
ritual.WyrmbloodTincture.name: Wyrmblood Tincture
temple.message.01: The passage seals behind you. Before you stand ancient ruins, their doorway carved with the same marks you saw in your dreams. Before you touch the door, the markings seem to stir. Aldric should hear about this before you venture farther.
temple.message.02: A surviving inscription warns that sacrifice was never measured in coin. The western shrine calls for three witnesses: something that drinks sunlight, something that once drew breath, and something hidden beneath stone. A fourth recess is shaped for a vial. The inscription beneath it reads: ‘Blood made portable is still blood.’
temple.message.03: The eastern tablets describe a boundary, not a distance. Solar essence marked one edge; void essence marked the other. The cult used bone to bind the two sides. The final recess is shaped for Blood Essence, linking the offering to a living hand.
temple.riddle.04: The central inscription reads: ‘Stone remembers the hand. Blood remembers the _____.’ What completes the line?
tome.001: The Red Passage is repeatable, even on a ritual day.
tome.002: The Call is exempt from the daily limit.
tome.003: The Rite of Severance is also exempt.
tome.006: The Sacrificial Altar is where rites are performed. Select a ritual there to see its full offerings, cost, and requirements.
tome.007: Ordinary rites consume Blood Essence, gold, and material offerings, but do not deduct health. Most can be performed once per day.
tome.008: Tier I teaches the hand to hold steady. Tier II reaches farther. Tier III invites powers that may answer on their own. Forbidden pages reveal themselves only when you learn their secrets.
tome.009: The pages record only what you have learned.

tome.018: The Rite of Severance has permanently ended the bond. No further Blood Debt can accrue, and old Blood Debt thresholds no longer bar learned rituals.
tome.019: Most rituals add one Blood Debt. As it accumulates, miscasts become more likely, and the valley may begin to answer your workings.
tome.020: One Lucky Lunch per day can reduce Blood Debt by one. Blood Debt rules can be adjusted in the mod settings.
tome.021: The altar menu lists consumed Essence, gold, and material offerings. No health is deducted by altar rites; the Blood Essence Harvester and the anchor offering are separate.
tome.023: [ Blood follows the line you draw. For now. ]
tome.025: [ The second mark reaches beyond the hand that made it. ]
tome.026: [ Sealed. Greater workings require Combat or Mining level 6. ]
tome.028: [ At the third mark, the darkness answers first. ]
tome.029: [ Sealed. The third tier requires Combat level 10. ]
tome.030: [ Alchemical mastery: 15% lower miscast chance (relative to the normal rate). ]
tome.038: Void Salt forms in places where life and shadow meet.
tome.039: It can be recovered from dangerous mine creatures, including shadow folk, serpents, bats, Squid Kids, and spiders. Krobus sometimes has a supply.
tome.040: The stronger the rite, the more carefully its salt must be measured.
tome.043: These rites are not mastered by skill alone. Their offerings are written plainly. Their other terms are not.
tome.046: Every working leaves a mark. These pages record more than your instructions: they record how much of you can be seen from the other side.
tome.047: [ You can close the cover. It does not close the correspondence. ]
tome.051: Blood does not open this passage. It reminds the stones of a route they once guarded. Follow it to the forgotten sanctuary.
tome.052: Travel rite: repeatable, even on the same day. No Blood Debt is added.
tome.053: [ You have walked the path. The stone remembers. ]
tome.056: The old practitioners opened a breach and failed to close it. Their records describe an anchor and the thing they hoped to control.
tome.057: Aldric is comparing the temple records with the recovered artifacts. You must wait for his findings.

tome.064: The diary preserves the sequence the cult failed to complete. The dagger can cut the anchor; Aldric's Field Sample steadies the passage. Once the threshold opens, there may be no turning back.
tome.065: [ The anchor has been broken. The knowledge remains. ]

tome.073: Something survived the battle: a claim upon your blood. This rite severs that final connection.
tome.074: Effect: permanently clears Blood Debt and prevents future gains. Your learned rituals remain.
tome.075: [ No workings have yet revealed themselves. ]
tome.076: Mark the soil with a measured drop of blood. Moonlight carries the working into root and leaf for a single day.
tome.077: Draw the ward close to the skin. Its sigils take the weight of a blow before flesh and bone must bear it.
tome.078: Call a shadow that is not cast by your body. It stays a step ahead, guiding your foot and blade toward fortunate openings.
tome.079: Tie your pulse to the striking hand. Something in the dark keeps time with it, lending force to every blow.
tome.080: Offer a taste of the earth's hidden seams. The stone answers, drawing strength and buried riches toward your grasp.
tome.081: At the final stroke of the sigil, the darkness arrives before it is called. It moves behind your eyes, bending blade and fortune to its will.
tome.082: Steep root and fang in living blood. The tincture wakes the muscles with a heat that does not belong to them.
tome.083: Steep moonberry and nightcap under a covered flame. The draught makes the currents of water and chance easier to follow.
tome.084: Bind a wandering soul to a sealed vessel. It follows just ahead, tugging at stray fortunes and things beyond your reach.
tome.085: Coax a buried ember until it answers. It learns the shape of your hand and teaches each strike a crueler force.
tome.086: No metal turns to gold. Instead, every skill in the caster awakens at once, answering a voice that sounds almost like their own.
tome.087: Mark the furrows with the same sign that wards a blade. The crops rise strong, yet every stalk leans toward you as though waiting for another offering.
tome.088: Do not seek the creature in this dream. Borrow its speed and sharpened instinct; it will borrow the shape of your fear.
tome.089: Promise the buried earth a share of what it gives. The seams open and the waters yield; above them, the moon keeps count.
tome.090: Leave the wound open when the sigil closes. The altar lends speed and violence, but the body is left easier to break.
tome.091: Feed the soil until its roots begin to reach for more. The fields flourish, but luck recoils from the hunger beneath them.
tome.092: Beneath a sun that casts no light, strength, speed, and fortune answer as one. The sigil closes like a mouth around the name of its maker.
tome.chrome.03: A record of blood, debt, and doors best left closed.
tome.chrome.04: Some passages do not appear until the tome decides you are ready to read them.
